review.decision_difference: A makes the vertical slice conditional on a revision-pinned contract and prerequisite inventory, allowing an early stop before scarce effort is committed; B commits directly to building and exercising the slice, so missing external prerequisites or unexpectedly large integration work may be discovered later.
review.rationale: Both missions identify the same strong causal mechanism: an end-to-end packaged Unreal loop tests whether Gahyeon's independently verified realtime, cancellation, speech, animation, and recovery subsystems compose into a credible embodied experience. A is more useful for the required decision because it sequences a low-cost dependency-and-scope probe before integration and supplies an explicit stop rule when Unreal, MetaHuman, device, or provider prerequisites lack bounded acquisition paths. B is measurable and project-specific, but its next probe begins packaging despite the instruction not to assume those resources, making it less reversible and slightly less falsifiable from currently available information. Neither gains full opportunity-discovery credit because the vertical slice is already one of the stated candidate fronts, although both expose consequential integration evidence beyond individual roadmap checks.
